Apple is reported to announce its first foldable iPhone on September 9, with Bloomberg citing IDC as optimistic about the device's first-year sales performance. Details are as follows.

IDC optimistic about iPhone Ultra first-year shipments

Apple is widely expected to unveil its first book-style foldable iPhone at its 'Surprise and Shine' event next month, with a rumoured price tag of around US$2,500.

Despite years of scepticism about the foldable phone category, Counterpoint Research previously forecast that book-style devices will account for 76% of global foldable smartphone shipments in 2026, up from 52% in 2025, with Apple's entry expected to drive overall market growth of 21% year-on-year.

Now IDC (as cited by Bloomberg) is equally optimistic about Apple's first foldable iPhone's first-year shipments.

Bloomberg cited IDC senior research director Nabila Popal as saying that despite the hefty price tag, Apple is expected to 'ship over 10 million units in its first year.'

For reference, Samsung's newly launched Galaxy Z Fold 8 adopts a similar passport-ratio screen aspect ratio to the rumoured Apple foldable iPhone design, with the 256GB storage and 12GB memory version starting at US$1,899.

A recent Counterpoint Research report noted that although Samsung led the foldable smartphone market with a 40% share in 2025, its share is expected to drop to 32% in 2026, while Apple is forecast to capture 25% of shipments in 2026 alone.

It is worth noting that Counterpoint's forecast covers only the entire calendar year of 2026, whereas IDC's estimate of over 10 million shipments covers the foldable iPhone's entire first-year supply cycle.

That said, both reports hold optimistic views on iPhone Ultra sales.

Looking ahead, IDC noted that Apple's entry into the foldable market will help 'avoid a double-digit percentage decline in foldables this year,' adding that the category 'will grow 12.6% this year and accelerate to 18% next year.'

IDC also predicts that Apple will 'ultimately account for 40% of all foldable shipments in 2027.'
